question: When the frozen classifier's top class is wrong on sampled tiny TAL positives, is the target often retained in its top three classes, and can its prediction-only top-two gap separate correct from wrong rows?
data: All previously fixed 512 fitting and 128 head-monitor train images. Report separately. Main subset: tiny TAL positives with reconstructed maximum sigmoid score>=0.25.
reconstruction: Read archived FP16 penultimate features and initial FP16 detector weights stored as FP32. Compute level-specific FP32 linear logits on CPU. This is an approximate diagnostic, not exact live detector replay.
metrics: Correct target class rank, top-three coverage among wrong rows, top1-vs-top2 logit-gap AUROC for correct-vs-wrong rows, counts and TAL-quality-weighted variants.
budget: Cache reads plus 3870-parameter frozen projections only. No images, detector forward, fitting, threshold search, new action execution or official evaluator.
pass_action: Only permits a separately registered detection-level raw-posterior audit. TAL samples are biased and have no final detection ownership, so this result alone never permits large training.
limits: Repeatedly viewed train scenes; detector trained on all of them. TAL quality is not GT IoU accuracy. No object/view IDs retained. Top-k availability is not deployable correction or AP. Soft classification fusion is established prior art, not a novelty claim. Original class-margin STOP remains.
